leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Imperatives
leadIn.content: Giving instructions or directions: Open your books, listen carefully, and do not talk during the test.

instructionCheck.question: Do you give directions turn-by-turn to your partner using imperatives?

meaningCheck.question: Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Imperatives?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · This structure provides explicit grammatical function and clarity.

meaningCheck.question: Form check: Does correct usage of Imperatives require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Accurate form and agreement choices prevent misunderstandings.

form.title: Form & Structure: Imperatives
form.content: Affirmative: Base verb (Open the door!). Negative: Don't + base verb (Don't touch that!).

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Notes: Imperatives
pronunciation.content: Spoken stress, weak forms, intonation, and articulation patterns for Imperatives.

controlledPractice.question: Which is a correct instruction?
controlledPractice.explanation: Imperatives drop the subject and use the base verb: Close the door.

controlledPractice.question: Negative imperative: '___ touch that.'
controlledPractice.explanation: Negative imperatives use Don't + base verb.

controlledPractice.question: Imperatives are mainly used for:
controlledPractice.explanation: Imperatives give instructions, rules, directions and recipes.
